title: IPR / patent portfolio management
holders: Wellspring for Tech Transfer; Helikon Labs; Commercify; SINT.OTRI; Protrak (ProrIISe); Inpart; KampusCore (TTO module); KSS TechTracS; IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS

phase11_effect: ESI (ipr=3) and IncuMan (ipr=2) both joined in Phase 11.

title: TRL as a first-class, reportable object
note: 2 of 40 build TRL natively (Inpart, IncuMan); 5 more partially. Wider than GAP-03 by one vendor and structurally different: it needs no scheme integration to be useful, and it is the object a NIRF or IIC return actually asks for.
phase11_effect: IncuMan arrived with trl=3. Moved from 1 of 28 to 2 of 40.

title: YUKTI-NIR / IIC / ARIIA submission workflow
holders: IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS; CSM Technologies (STPI CoE)
joined: IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS; CSM Technologies (STPI CoE)
note: WAS 'Zero of 29 competitors. Highest-value and most-defensible gap in the category.' Now 3 of 40 - all three Phase 11 discoveries, none with a named customer. IncuMan is private beta; ESI publishes a compliance export carrying a live '(TODO)'; CSM Technologies is a government systems integrator, not a product. Zero partial implementations, which means nobody has solved the easy version either.
phase11_effect: THE MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE IN THE STUDY. Not closed - contested by entrants with no customer proof.

title: Unified mandate-spanning reporting
holders: NestLens Orbit; EcoSync; Accubate; VentureLink; Gohorto; AcceleratorApp; IdeaScale; Envisio; Wazoku; Dealum; FIKR; FosiaHub; European Startup Hub; Catalyzer; Wellspring for Tech Transfer; Helikon Labs; Commercify; SINT.OTRI; Elsevier Pure; Protrak (ProrIISe); Inpart; KSS TechTracS; Startup Science; Babele; Octorank SRM; IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS; CSM Technologies (STPI CoE)
joined: IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS; CSM Technologies (STPI CoE)
note: RETIRED by Rule 1. 28 of 40 vendors build reporting natively or better; exactly 1 has it absent. Reporting is the most saturated capability in the category. It cannot be a differentiator and should not appear in a feature roadmap as one.
phase11_effect: Phase 11 found no institutional user complaining about reporting. The spec's own example table proposed 'Reporting -> Automated' as a differentiator; that is wrong.

title: Government-grant disbursement ledger traced to a receipt
holders: NestLens Orbit; EcoSync; IncubatX; VentureLink; AcceleratorApp; Dealum; KSS TechTracS; Startup Science; Crino; IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS
joined: NestLens Orbit; EcoSync; VentureLink; AcceleratorApp; Dealum; KSS TechTracS; Startup Science; IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS
note: 11 of 40 build funding natively and 10 more partially. NestLens Orbit, IncubatX, VentureLink and AcceleratorApp all do grant tracking; ESI and IncuMan both carry a grant pipeline. A plain grant ledger is now table stakes. What is NOT built is tracing a disbursement to a receipt and to the scheme's utilisation format (NIDHI-SSS, DST-TBI, BIRAC) - though Orbit already ships those report formats.
phase11_effect: ESI and IncuMan both added grant pipelines.

title: Faculty, Innovation Ambassadors and the non-startup innovator
note: NOT MEASURED as a Phase 10 dimension, so no honest count exists. Phase 9 scored 'faculty' as a feature flag: it is held by tech-transfer platforms and by ZERO incubation platforms, all of which build intake from 'startup application'. Phase 1 evidence is strong and independent - 15,000 college Innovation Ambassadors, 25,000 school ambassadors, and institutions splitting innovation funding three ways (innovation / startup / IPR). The 12 vendors added after Phase 9 were NOT scored on this axis, which is a gap in the matrix rather than a fact about them.
phase11_effect: Not re-checked. Flagged as an unmeasured axis.

title: Mentor logistics at scale - NDA-tiered visibility
holders: NestLens Orbit; IncubatX; Accubate; Founderhood; VentureLink; RiserNest; Gohorto; FIKR; European Startup Hub; Catalyzer; Startup Science; Babele; IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS; CSM Technologies (STPI CoE)
joined: NestLens Orbit; IncubatX; Accubate; Founderhood; VentureLink; RiserNest; Gohorto; FIKR; European Startup Hub; Catalyzer; Startup Science; Babele; IncuMan; ESI Incubation Centre OS; CSM Technologies (STPI CoE)
note: 15 of 40 build mentorship natively, 11 partially - the category's third most saturated capability. The surviving claim is narrow: visibility tiered by NDA plus mentor hours logged against scheme utilisation. incuTrack sells mentor matching as a PAID ADD-ON, which is the clearest signal that the category treats mentorship as an accessory.

title: AI that is auditable instead of just advertised
holders: IncubatX; IdeaScale; Wazoku; Dealum; FIKR; FosiaHub; Startup Science; Crino; Babele
joined: IncubatX; IdeaScale; Wazoku; Dealum; FIKR; FosiaHub; Startup Science; Crino; Babele
note: 9 of 40 build AI natively, 9 partially, 21 absent. Phase 11 is the decisive input: NOT ONE user in the retrieved corpus asked for AI. Phase 11 explicitly listed 'nobody has solved AI-driven incubation' as NOT SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE. The auditable framing survives on VentureLink (logs every score change with actor, value and reason) and on EcoSync's refusal to publish AI scores at all - two opposing proofs that the audit trail, not the model, is the thing worth building.
phase11_effect: Downgraded from a feature to a posture.

title: Unincorporated pre-incubation state
note: 0 of 40, and no vendor even partially attempts it. Every platform assumes a registered entity with a DPIIT number and a cap table. Phase 1 shows why that is wrong for this buyer: NIT Calicut's report attributes 38 of 55 incubated ventures to an undefined 'others' bucket, 94 activities produced 0 IPs, and 843 ideas came from just 42 activities. The university's funnel is overwhelmingly PRE-entity.
phase11_effect: Not re-checked. Strongest Phase 1 support of the seven.

title: Guaranteed migration off forms/spreadsheets/WhatsApp
note: Every vendor CLAIMS migration. Zero sells it as a guaranteed, scoped engagement with the data carried over - which is the only part the buyer cares about. Phase 11 sharpened this into something bigger than a feature: the displaced incumbent is Google Forms and spreadsheets (two Accubate reviewers name Google Forms explicitly), and the real blocker is inertia, which nobody in the category addresses because the people who feel it never go looking for software.
phase11_effect: Promoted from a feature to the wedge strategy.

title: Departments and multi-campus sub-tenancy
note: Multi-site is becoming table stakes (Accubate Enterprise, VentureLink, NestLens Orbit). What is absent is sub-tenancy per DEPARTMENT with a departmental P&L and correct SPV-versus-department IP ownership - which is how Indian universities are actually organised. Phase 9's 'multisite' flag cannot distinguish the two, so this is asserted from Phase 9's narrative rather than counted. A known limitation of the matrix.

title: Deployment model an Indian university can actually buy
note: Real but not a product differentiator - it is a packaging decision. Phase 8 supplies the proof: Fedena sells a FULL college ERP at Rs 1,00,000 flat with unlimited users, below StartupHub's recommended Rs 1.2 lakh list. Univation offers a directly comparable platform FREE to universities with Google Ads credit. Free is an active price in this market and the entry shape is a requirement, not an advantage.
phase11_effect: Unchanged. Phase 11 found a second free competitor.

title: A verifiable Indian reference institution
note: Protrak/ProrIISe at IISc remains the ONLY named Indian university deployment in 40 vendors - and it is IP management, not incubation. Phase 11 found no Indian university reference for IncuMan, ESI or CSM. EcoSync's TBI-KIET is a vendor claim. The gap survives for INCUBATION, where the reference is the thing a committee actually asks for.
phase11_effect: Confirmed against the 4 new vendors; all three have none.
